title: Indexed supported homogeneous division for an ordered monomial diagram
statement:
For a finite linearly ordered variable set $S$ and a finite linearly ordered vertex index set $I$, use the exponent vectors $\mathbf N^S$, the polynomial ring $A[Y_j:j\in S]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and its canonical inclusion into formal series [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. An additive monotone diagram is a set $D\subset\mathbf N^S$ with $a+b\in D$ for all $a\in D,b\in\mathbf N^S$, closed under $a\mapsto a-a_i e_i+a_i e_j$ for $i<j$. An ordered vertex family $a:I	o\mathbf N^S$ enumerates exactly the coordinatewise minimal elements of $D$ in strictly ascending degree-lexicographic order $(|a|,(a_j)_{j\in S})$. Write $\langle aangle=\{e:\exists i, a_i\le e\}$ and $\Delta_i=\{b: orall h<i,\ a_h
ot\le a_i+b\}$. For a commutative ring $A$ and polynomials $H_i$, define the degree-$t$ index set as the disjoint union of the pairs $(i,b)$ with $b\in\Delta_i$, $|b|+|a_i|=t$, and the exponents $e
otin D$ with $|e|=t$. The indexed family sends these to $Y^bH_i$ and $Y^e$, respectively. It spans degree $t$ if its $A$-linear span equals the homogeneous degree-$t$ submodule. Unique supported homogeneous division in degree $t$ means that every homogeneous degree-$t$ polynomial has unique finitely supported $A$-coefficients in this indexed family. Grouping the coefficients with fixed $i$ gives the quotient polynomial supported in $\Delta_i$, and the remaining coefficients give the remainder outside $D$. Say that $b\in\mathbf N$ is a finite division test for $(D,a,A)$ if, for every family $H_i$ homogeneous of degrees $|a_i|$: (i) spanning at $q\ge b$ implies spanning at every $t\ge q$; (ii) in every degree the indexed family is linearly independent whenever it spans; (iii) spanning in every degree at most $b$ is equivalent to unique supported homogeneous division in every degree. The degree prefix at $d$ restricts the vertex index set to $\{i:|a_i|\le d\}$ with its inherited order and uses the diagram it generates. Essential variables are $\{j:\exists i,a_i(j)
e0\}$; restriction deletes all other coordinates of each vertex and uses the diagram generated by the resulting vertices. These definitions include empty sets and the zero ring.
